A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLaVA-Video research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables and equations, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, dataset ablations, frame/token experiments and qualitative model outputs in Tables 2–4 and 8–13.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies and adds TemporalBench results in Table 2.

M1.justification: The three-level captioning pipeline, QA generation/filtering, model architecture and SlowFast pooling procedure remain unchanged. The corrected token-count equation aligns with pooling already specified in v1; it does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Section 4 and Table 2 add TemporalBench for fine-grained temporal understanding. The training sources, training mixture and previously evaluated benchmarks are retained; the shortened category chart does not establish removed training domains.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds VideoLLaMA2-72B and removes GPT-4V and Gemini-1.5-Flash. VILA-40B and LongVA-7B entries move from the LongVideoBench comparison to VideoDC. The dataset-comparison and video-representation comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added TemporalBench evaluation introduces reporting labelled m-acc in Table 2. Retained benchmarks keep their reported splits and main model configurations. Removal of explicit ablation-configuration statements does not establish that those experimental settings changed.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 revise baseline evidence in the existing analyses of training-mixture benefits and dataset quality, without adding new ablation designs. Figure 7 narrows the category-distribution analysis. The historical-context comparison, frame/token studies and capability cases remain intact.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The parenthetical values removed from Table 4 were performance differences, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes LLaVA-Hound's NExT-QA score from 48.2 to 64.4. Table 4 replaces its NExT-QA/PerceptionTest/EgoSchema/VideoMME scores of 64.4/51.4/51.0/51.0 with 39.8/53.1/25.8/55.2, reversing the reported EgoSchema ranking against the unchanged 49.8. Table 2 adds TemporalBench scores of 22.9 and 33.7 for LLaVA-Video-7B/72B and reassigns VILA/LongVA's 3.37/3.14 entries from LongVideoBench to VideoDC. These materially revise empirical comparisons, although the proposed models' scores on retained benchmarks and Tables 8–9 remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain whether the replaced scores reflect corrections or changed experiments.

T1.justification: Section 4 and the SlowFast appendix correct the fast-frame token-count term from M/p² to M/(4p²), consistent with the stated 2p-by-2p pooling. No new theorem, proof or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: the synthetic instruction dataset, LLaVA-Video models, dense temporal sampling and efficient SlowFast representation. The additional evaluation does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds concerns about source-platform biases and annotator-dependent QA skew. Section 3.4 removes explanations connecting short-video and comedy predominance to YouTube Shorts and view-based selection. Interpretations of the main benchmark and frame-sampling results otherwise remain.

D1.justification: v3 removes the explicit V=(64,679,1,2) configuration statements for Sections 4.2–4.3, the in-house tagging-model description and the front-page project link. Main model configurations, hardware information and generation prompts remain. These are documentation losses, not demonstrated changes to implementation or resource availability.

R1.justification: Related work adds VideoReCap and distinguishes the proposed pipeline through historical conditioning of clip-level captions. References for TemporalBench and VideoLLaMA2 are added, while InsTag is removed with its accompanying discussion. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. The title gains the LLaVA-Video prefix, dataset-statistics discussion is shortened, limitations and acknowledgements are added, and the author-contributions appendix is removed, shifting the remaining appendix labels.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout into TMLR style, changing the author block, headers, typography, margins and figure/table placement. Tables 3–4 become compact displays with rotated headings, Table 4 loses displayed differences, and Table 2 gains a column. Figure 7 shrinks from four example strips and ten category bars to two strips and five bars.

improvement.justification: TemporalBench, clearer positioning against VideoReCap and the corrected token-count formula are useful gains. However, large baseline-score replacements are unexplained and ablation settings are less explicit. Table 3 now implies a 15.7-point NExT-QA gain while the text retains 31.9; the Gemini-1.5-Flash parity claim also remains after its comparison row is removed. The PDFs cannot establish whether the revised scores correct earlier errors, and the benefits coexist with new reporting inconsistencies, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
